lesson_title: Photo Day: Year-End, the Gauges and the Guards
hook_text: Before the photo, you tidy the room. That's the whole secret of year-end.
clip_script: Year-end in Accounting is photo day — one picture of the business at midnight on the last day, and outsiders have to trust it. But nobody photographs an untidy room. The bakkie in the yard isn't worth what it cost — the books must admit the wearing: depreciation, truth arriving with no cash moving. February's electricity, billed in March? It belongs in THIS picture — pull it in. Insurance paid ahead for next year? Push it out — that cover is something the shop still owns. Rent the tenant hasn't paid yet? Earned this year — pull it in. Four moves, one principle: the photo shows what the year truly used and truly earned, not what the bank account happened to see. Skip the tidying and the photo lies — richer than real, or poorer. Then two documents leave photo day: the report card, telling how the year went — and the health check, the ratios, telling how the body is doing underneath. Tidy, photograph, read. That's year-end.
visual_style: A cluttered shop room snapping tidy item by item — a bakkie fading slightly, bills flying in, a paid-ahead policy flying out — then a camera flash freezing a balanced statement; a report card and a stethoscope appearing as the two outputs.
pacing: Four quick tidy-up beats, one flash, two-document landing.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision session and take an honest photo.
